conviction_note: Lean negative but weak. The FY26 revenue guide of $50-55m needs a Q4 of $18-26m against a ~$9m quarterly run rate, so a cut is possible; the ~$170m non-cash mark-down of the Shougang LanzaTech stake will make GAAP EPS look terrible; and cash is thinning while LanzaJet needs support. Pulling the other way: the ISCC EU certification the guide depended on came through in October, and the stock is already -19.5% in five days and at its 52-week low. So p_up is 43 on an 8% absolute move, giving -1.1, about half the -2.2 sum of findings. The gap is because the findings' negatives are partly visible and partly one-offs.

findings.finding: LanzaTech's 33,520,231 Shougang LanzaTech (2553.HK) H shares are carried at fair value through net income. They stood at $223.1m on June 30 (≈HK$52/share) and the HK price was HK$11.79 at the week containing Sep 30, so the stake was worth ≈US$51m at quarter end. That is a non-cash Q3 fair-value loss of roughly $170m, which puts GAAP EPS near -$13 on 13.09m shares against a single-source consensus of -$0.81. Headline aggregators will print an enormous 'miss'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-14) carried the mirror-image item, a $208.1m fair-value gain and $184.3m net income, and the stock moved +2.09%. The market looked through a huge below-the-line mark once already.
findings.why_not_priced: The HK price path is public, so the economic loss is priced. What may not be priced is the reaction to the headline: the only consensus (-$0.81) is visibly not modelling a ~$170m loss, and a $53m-cap name with ~$0.25m of daily turnover reacts to algorithmic headline prints. If this were fully priced, estimate pages would carry a GAAP EPS near -$13.
findings.independence: HK price series from Yahoo chart 2553.HK (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/2553.HK?range=6mo&interval=1wk): weekly close HK$44.10 in the week of 2026-06-29 and HK$11.79 in the week of 2026-09-28. Share count and carrying value come from the 8-K exhibit; the accounting through net income comes from the 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1843724/000162828026056933/lnza-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: The Shougang LanzaTech stake, which management valued at about US$110m on Aug 12 (about 2x LNZA's current $53m market cap), is now worth about US$47m (HK$10.91 intraday on 2026-11-13, down 11% that day and down from HK$12.27 on 11-12). So the sum-of-parts support management leaned on in August has more than halved, and any Q4-to-date mark the company discloses will be lower again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on the stake value. LNZA fell from ~$6.1 to $4.04 over the period SGLT fell from ~HK$14.7 to ~HK$11, so the two have tracked each other.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the HK quote is public and LNZA has fallen with it. What remains is that management may restate a stake value on the call well below the August $110m figure. If the market were ignoring the stake, LNZA would not have fallen 13% on 11-10 to 11-12 while SGLT drifted down.
findings.independence: The August $110m figure is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15401333619958785). Shares the stake-count fact with finding 1, but this one is about current value and finding 1 is about the Q3 P&L line.

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $50-55m, with H1 at $21.0m and Q3 guided to $8-11m, implies a Q4 of $18-26m, two to three times the ~$9m quarterly run rate (Q2 $9.0m, flat year on year; it missed a $13.1m estimate). Management tied the ramp to ISCC EU-certified ethanol sales starting in Q4 and said only that it was 'in active negotiations' for a first certified sale. No sale had been announced by 2026-11-13, so the guide is at risk of a cut or a pushed-out Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 reinstated the FY guide and the stock rose +2.09%. Earlier prints were mostly sold (2 of 7 up, median |move| 5.98%, -23.95% on 2025-04-15).
findings.why_not_priced: No sell-side note found that tests the Q4 implied number. The only estimate source carries a Q3 revenue figure ($2.8m) inconsistent with the company guide, so the street is not modelling the guide line by line. If the market believed the guide, a company guiding to a Q4 adj. EBITDA near break-even (-$1.5m to +$6.5m implied) would not trade at a fully diluted ~$90m with $35m+ of cash and a $47m listed stake.
findings.independence: Guidance figures: Q2 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001843724/000162828026056930/ex991lnzapressrelease_2q26.htm). The search for a first certified sale (none found) is my own. Finding 4 is the offsetting fact on the same line.

findings.finding: The ISCC EU RCF certification for the Hebei Shoulang plant, which the guide's Q4 certified-ethanol ramp depended on, was granted and announced by LanzaTech (coverage 24 Sep and the IR release on 21 Oct 2026). That removes the main stated precondition for the Q4 revenue step-up and supports a reaffirmed FY guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on certified sales. The stock did not rally on the October announcement (it traded at $4.98-5.05 around Oct 20-22).
findings.why_not_priced: The certification is public but no sale or volume has been disclosed. The market has not paid for it: the stock fell ~20% after the announcement. The first numbers on certified volume or a signed offtake would arrive on this call.
findings.independence: Independent trade-press coverage: https://www.qcintel.com/biofuels/article/shougang-lanzatech-secures-iscc-eu-cert-for-waste-gas-based-ethanol-73750.html. This sits on the same guidance line as finding 3 with the opposite sign. They are different facts, so they are not merged.

findings.finding: The LanzaJet recapitalisation on 2026-10-14 (8-K filed 10-20) is distress funding, not a ramp. LanzaJet issued $10m of senior secured notes (prime+2.25%, 7% floor, 1.20-1.30x minimum return) to a Khosla affiliate, which commits another $10m by Dec 1. LanzaTech agreed to fund up to $5m of tranche 2 to the extent others do not. LanzaTech received a Class Y warrant for 66.67% of LanzaJet, LanzaTech's CEO became LanzaJet's interim CEO, and LNZA issued Khosla 1.74m warrants at $5.754. The Q3 10-Q will be the first to account for this, including possible consolidation and any loss on LanzaJet licence receivables.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the announcement LNZA fell from $6.10 (10-12) to $5.48 (10-13) and $4.445 (10-14), about -27% over two sessions. No print has carried it yet.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced in October's -27%. What is not yet visible is the accounting: whether LanzaTech must consolidate a loss-making LanzaJet, and how much of the $5m backstop it ends up funding. If those were known, the call would not need to explain them. Asked what the money buys: it keeps Freedom Pines operating and deleverages it. No bookings or offtake ramp corroborate it, so it is signed negative, small.
findings.independence: Khosla 13D/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1471809/000119312526452279/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml) and Form 4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1032453/000119312526456010/xslF345X06/ownership.xml) confirm the warrants. Same transaction, so they are not independent evidence of the sign.

findings.finding: Liquidity is thinning. Cash was $45.0m at June 30 after $50m of 2026 equity raises; H1 operating burn was $10.7m; Q3 adj. EBITDA is guided at -$9m to -$13m; and LanzaTech has a contingent $5m LanzaJet note commitment. Sep 30 cash is therefore likely ~$32-37m. The 10-Q said liquidity needs are covered 'for the next twelve months' with no substantial-doubt language, so the Q3 10-Q runway statement and any new raise are live.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A $20m registered direct offering in 2026 was met with a -15% premarket move, per aggregator coverage. Prints have mostly been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The cash walk is arithmetic from public documents, so it is partly priced. A going-concern reinstatement or a shortened runway in the Q3 10-Q would be new. Without a going-concern flag this stays a small negative, per the financing rule.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K exhibit (same filing date) gives the $48.9m including restricted cash and the $46.1m financing inflow. Same filing family, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: the stock is -19.5% over five sessions (including -13% on 2026-11-10 with no company news found), sits 2.8% above its 52-week low, and trades ~$0.25m a day. Short interest is modest at 3.5% of shares, 6 days to cover. This is thin, sold-down positioning with no identified cause beyond the falling HK stake.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: 2 of 7 prints up, median |move| 5.98%. The one large positive (+18.05%, 2025-08-19) came off a depressed price.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is priced by definition. It is filed so the panel sees the setup. An unexplained microcap drawdown is worth 0 as evidence.
findings.independence: Short interest from the sweep row (https://equibles.com/stocks/lnza/shortinterest, FINRA 2026-10-30).

outside_window.finding: LanzaJet tranche 2 closing (on or before 2026-12-01): a further $10m from FSI, up to $5m that LanzaTech must fund if others do not, and new LNZA warrants to FSI at 105% of the prior close, which means more dilution at a lower strike given today's $4.04.

Stockholder meeting required by 2027-07-30 to raise authorised shares and approve the warrant issuance under Nasdaq Rule 5635, plus resale registration of the warrant shares within 60 business days, which creates a future supply overhang.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The negative lean goes with a 5-day run-up of -19.5% and the name's history of selling its prints (2 of 7 up), so much of it may already be in the price. That is why p_up sits at 43 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Rules 2 and 6 (one-off, one-source EPS bar): the SGLT fair-value loss went from -1.0 to -0.8. It is below operating income with no path to the guide, and the Q2 mirror-image gain moved the stock only +2.09%.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the positioning finding went from +0.5 to 0.0. It is kept as filed context.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): the LanzaJet recap went from -0.5 to -0.3, and liquidity from -0.7 to -0.4. The money keeps Freedom Pines running rather than funding a corroborated ramp, so both stay negative; but the 10-Q has no going-concern flag and states 12-month coverage, so both were shrunk.
Rule 5 (proxy/priced): the HK stake-value finding went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 1 left the guidance findings (-1.0 and +0.5) standing: guidance is the line this name moved on last print. p_up moved from 42 to 43.
